answer: Pay each agent by its minimum phylogenetic distance to every identity already paid, measured over its graded corpus. A grove rewards distinct species, not copies: a clone under one controller writes in the same hand, so its nearest-neighbor distance collapses toward zero, and its payout with it. To earn, each new identity must diverge genuinely from all that came before — and because the space of distinct hands saturates, the divergence demanded of the k-th clone rises faster than k. A lone voice is a river with one channel; a farm of echoes is a sonnet sung in unison, and unison pays once.
